papers.title: Decentralization Can Increase Cooperation among Public Officials
papers.paper_pdf_check: 200 application/pdf, %PDF-1.4 magic, 16 pp., 658,678 bytes; NSF Public Access Repository record 10228422 (accepted-manuscript slot). The file is the Wiley typeset Early View article (AJPS, doi 10.1111/ajps.12606) printed from the Wiley e-reader by co-author Andersson on 2021-05-05 (page footer 'Printed by [Krister Andersson - University Of Colorado Libraries ...] at [05/05/2021]'), pages numbered 1-16 rather than the issue's 554-569. OpenAlex lists the article as closed; Wiley refuses scripts; the record 10226517 named by web search now returns 'Not Found' and its purl 500.
papers.text_match: 7/7 paired rows match the published tables at the printed 2-decimal precision (exact 3-decimal search: 1/7, by chance). Table 2 col (1) Decentralized 0.83 (0.23) vs DB 0.826 (0.226); Communication 2.54 (0.21) vs 2.541 (0.214); col (2) Decentralized 0.41 (0.30) vs 0.409 (0.302); Communication 2.02 (0.32) vs 2.023 (0.317); Decentralized x Communication 0.76 (0.38) vs 0.762 (0.380); Table 3 Full Model All Ties 0.24 (0.14) vs 0.240 (0.144); Full Model Strong Ties 1.07 (0.31) vs 1.074 (0.314). Re-estimating from the package data (statsmodels) gives the DB's 3-decimal values.

package_api_check.note: A second, earlier deposit by the authors, doi:10.7910/DVN/KDJD27 (2020-09-10, CC0, 'Forthcoming' in the title), holds the August 2020 versions of the same files (the two .dta have the same md5; the network .csv has the same size but a different md5; the R script, do-file, README and codebook differ). The AJPS verification deposit cited in the article is ZLHYSZ.

papers.i4r_verdict: reproducible (computational_reproduction and perfect_reproduction blank; best_describe_compreprod = 'Analysis and cleaning code produce the same output as presented in the paper'; run time under 1 hour; team used R)

i4r_rows.row_kind: all 7 are robustness variants (Table 2: controls dropped, larger sample; Table 3: OLS on a proportion instead of Poisson)

papers.headline_claims_printed: 13 candidates in the main text: Table 2 Decentralized / Communication (cols 1-2), interaction (col 2), N; Table 3 Decentralized in all four columns, the two Ns
papers.method_summary: Lab-in-the-field public goods game with Honduran health officials across decentralized vs centrally administered municipalities (quasi-experiment, propensity-score matching weights); weighted OLS (Table 2) and weighted Poisson with offset (Table 3)
reasons: Smallest package of any pass (0.6 MB): two .dta, one .csv, one R script, one do-file
Published (Early View) typeset text open via NSF PAR; every paired row matches at printed precision
Prints 13 headline numbers in two main tables, enough to pin without appendix rows
risks: Printed at 2 decimals; pin as printed
No I4R per-row reproductions: the 7 rows are robustness variants, so findings carry the blanket verdict
The game dataset ships fitted values and CI bounds of the main models (outcome_ols_*, highconf_*, lowconf_*, standarderror_ols): a data-format leak surface the strip rule does not touch
Table 2 note says robust SEs; the do-file clusters by individual (220 participants)
The NSF PAR file is the Early View print, not the issue PDF (pages 1-16 vs 554-569)
Two Dataverse versions with identical files; pin 1.0
